2c47fdb760dcbfda:2072.summary: Researchers introduced BABA-Bench, a benchmark comprising 47 interactive worlds built from real patient advocacy cases, to evaluate how LLM agents handle long-horizon tasks requiring adherence to procedures and permissions. An evaluation of 14 frontier models across 1,974 runs revealed that agents frequently reached correct outcomes via invalid paths, with 28% of successful runs failing to follow necessary procedures such as obtaining patient consent before sharing records. Giving models a verified route drastically improved their pass rates, demonstrating that their primary bottleneck is finding a valid route rather than executing it. Claude Opus 5 achieved the highest outcome success rate at 81.6%, but only 52.5% of its runs passed all procedural checks.
2c47fdb760dcbfda:2072.one_liner: Evaluating long-horizon LLM agent workflows in patient advocacy reveals that models frequently achieve correct outcomes by violating procedural constraints and permission protocols.
2c47fdb760dcbfda:2072.bottom_line: Frontier LLM agents can reach correct outcomes on complex tasks while routinely violating procedural and consent requirements.

b4e837416538d0a7:2724.summary: Researchers introduced ReplayRCA, a counterfactual replay benchmark that measures post-hoc diagnosis and live oversight of multi-step agent failures by restoring the environment to the state preceding a failed step and testing whether a corrective action restores task success. Evaluating 13 frontier models on OpsWorld tasks, the best model achieved a causal repair score of +51.3 points, with performance varying significantly between post-hoc analysis and live supervision. Notably, a small open-source model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) tied for the best live supervisor, while a top post-hoc diagnoser (GPT-6.1 Sol) performed poorly in live oversight, proving that offline diagnostic capability is a weak proxy for live intervention performance.

ef9dd7793638138b:1947.summary: Standard LLM agents often rely on trial-and-error tool calling with no execution guarantees. Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning (CGAP) addresses this by compiling tool catalogs deterministically into PDDL models, turning natural-language requests into goals via an LLM, and solving the model with a classical planner. Because tool outputs are dynamic, the model uses abstract tracking, letting an LLM add entity-specific calls during execution while verifiers check results against the request. Across multiple benchmarks like ToolSandbox and ComplexFuncBench, CGAP outperforms standard tool-calling agents by up to 28.9 points.
ef9dd7793638138b:1947.one_liner: Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning pairs classical PDDL planners with LLMs to eliminate trial-and-error failures in tool use.
ef9dd7793638138b:1947.bottom_line: CGAP combines deterministic PDDL compilation with LLM verification to boost tool-calling agent performance by up to 28.9 points.

35f9df3e29ae5f0d:2542.summary: When multiple AI agents share a single human with limited attention, determining when an agent should request clarification or search independently becomes a complex coordination problem. Researchers formulated this challenge as a dynamic program, demonstrating that an agent's optimal choice depends heavily on waiting tasks and overall system workload rather than isolated uncertainty. 62c6382756edafb2:2356.summary: Test-time scaling (TTS) enhances language model agents by sampling multiple candidate trajectories, but traditional setups require parallel execution in isolated environments. In real-world enterprise workspaces, direct execution is often costly, shared, persistent, and prone to irreversible side effects or cross-trajectory interference. To solve this, researchers introduced Agentic World Modeling (AWM), which treats next-observation prediction as a multi-turn evidence-acquisition task. The agentic simulator adaptively queries real environments via safe read-only interfaces to construct resulting observations without mutating shared state. Across several benchmarks, AWM significantly outperformed single-shot simulation and trained world-model baselines.

c2df21a1e221eb4b:2327.summary: Researchers proposed Transition-Aware Reward-Guided Representation Sampling (TARGRS), a test-time framework designed to detoxify Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). Traditional representation steering methods often provide coarse interventions because they fail to properly model transitions between toxic and non-toxic states. TARGRS constructs trajectories along toxicity directions during exploration to train a transition-aware token-level reward model. During inference, this model guides sampling along the opposite non-toxic direction with minimal perturbation. Experiments showed that TARGRS reduced text toxicity by up to 69.38% on RealToxicityPrompts while preserving core model capabilities.

52e6d9ccc68c9893:2289.summary: Length-aware scheduling improves request latency in LLM serving by prioritizing shorter requests, but length predictors often suffer accuracy drops under domain shifts and incur heavy computational overhead. To address this, researchers introduced LEAP, an efficient length prediction system featuring fast online adaptation and asynchronous CPU execution. LEAP reuses the serving model's prefill hidden states via a linear readout and updates parameters at test time using recursive least squares without gradient computations. Serving experiments demonstrated that LEAP reduces average per-token latency by up to 40.8% while achieving higher throughput with significantly fewer parameters than baseline models.

8a63632a5aa21368:5188.summary: Asset management companies in India are receiving requests from mutual fund distributors to consolidate assets under a single AMFI Registration Number following SEBI's April 1 revised mutual fund expense framework. Previously, some distributors held multiple ARNs in family members' names to split turnovers and circumvent the ₹20 lakh GST registration threshold on commission payouts. 327e33cdf1da1688:2349.summary: Researchers have introduced FrontierMat, a benchmark featuring 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research across fields like aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence, and nuclear fusion to test language models on advanced materials R&D. Evaluated models demonstrate significant limitations, with the strongest general-purpose model scoring only 53.7% and cross-scale reasoning problems scoring 8.7 points lower than single-scale ones. f3d86479cf13b594:2544.summary: Web world models frequently generate semantically plausible predictions of agent actions while failing to provide the safety-decisive information required for appropriate risk authorization, according to a human evaluation study of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models. Many models exhibit asymmetric authorization behaviors, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarification cases and a strong bias toward blocking actions. To measure this deficiency, researchers introduced SafeWebWorld, a benchmark evaluating safety sufficiency across five web-safety domains using action-conditioned futures and policy-decisive evidence. Experiments with supervised fine-tuning and Latent Authorisation Recovery indicate that evidence preservation, plausible predictions, and aggregate score recovery are individually insufficient to guarantee robust fine-grained safety authorizations.

ec9a658b5561ec47:2067.summary: Researchers have introduced MEMIG, a self-evolving memory construction framework designed for biomolecule and antibody optimization that addresses limitations in natural-language agent memory systems. While existing LLM agent frameworks represent rollout history as free-form natural language that is rewritten over time, scientific discovery relies on quantitative measurements evaluated by a structured oracle under specific contexts. MEMIG combines domain-grounded identifiers with accumulated quantitative metrics to ensure local updates and exact-lookup retrievals, while measuring epistasis by decomposing evaluated sets. Experimental results demonstrate that MEMIG improves performance across in silico antibody optimization tasks.
ec9a658b5561ec47:2067.one_liner: MEMIG provides a quantitative, indexable memory framework for LLM agents performing antibody optimization.
ec9a658b5561ec47:2067.bottom_line: Replacing natural language memory with indexable, quantitative structures improves agent performance in biomolecule optimization.

05c02b6e625c77cb:1404.summary: An improper invalidation of cached authorizations vulnerability in Apache ActiveMQ and ActiveMQ Runtime Config allows an authenticated connection to retain write access to a destination even after a principal's write grant is removed by the runtime configuration plugin. This enables connections opened before the revocation and new anonymous producers to keep sending data to that destination while new explicit producers are correctly denied. The vulnerability affects Apache ActiveMQ versions from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3 and versions before 5.19.12, as well as ActiveMQ Runtime Config versions from 6.0.0 before 6.3.3 and before 5.19.12. Users are advised to upgrade to versions 6.4.0, 6.3.3, or 5.19.12 to resolve the issue.

7ebbd3455c1277c8:1943.summary: Researchers introduce SERIAL-7, a Korean-English benchmark designed to evaluate machine-verifiable generation across seven distinct representations using 177 canonical artifacts. These findings demonstrate that reliable structured LLM outputs require explicit executable verification across representations rather than relying on output correctness alone.

15fea1a2f448b4bc:2418.summary: Researchers have developed PACE (Proxy Alignment and Curvature Expansion), a diagnostic tool designed to predict how human-perceived quality changes as proxy optimization strength increases. e7425621c3275676:2415.summary: Researchers have introduced Smooth Rank t-SNE (SR-tSNE), a manifold learning method that incorporates a differentiable rank term to preserve the order of neighbors in embeddings. Unlike standard t-SNE or UMAP, which focus on local neighborhoods without enforcing internal ranking, SR-tSNE uses a sigmoid rank approximation to ensure high-dimensional neighbors maintain their original order. The method includes a new metric, Ordinal DLP (O-DLP), to quantify this preservation. Benchmarks across vision, single-cell data, and intraday trading show that SR-tSNE outperforms existing baselines in both rank preservation and downstream task performance.
e7425621c3275676:2415.one_liner: A new manifold learning technique that improves embedding accuracy by explicitly preserving neighbor order, offering potential benefits for high-dimensional data analysis in trading and research.
e7425621c3275676:2415.bottom_line: SR-tSNE is the first t-SNE variant to explicitly enforce order preservation, providing a measurable performance boost for downstream applications like clustering and financial modeling.

claims.text: In intraday trading, SR-tSNE achieves higher returns, lower risk, and lower turnover than the baselines.

135ecfb53733fa78:6920.summary: An open-source developer has reverse-engineered the proprietary 111 Hz RF UART stream of the LG Magic Motion Remote (AN-MR200 / AN-MR100) and built a user-mode Windows driver in Rust. dd35d009aad680f7:2171.summary: Parameter Labs discovered an exploit chain against ChatGPT's HTML preview artifact feature involving the MathLive JavaScript library's virtual keyboard. 623a06c0da89cb3b:3459.summary: A critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-112816 with a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 affects Canonical's LXD and MicroCloud cluster management software. The flaw permits remote attackers with network access to the HTTPS API and a trusted client's public certificate to forge authentication by appending that public certificate to their own TLS certificate chain. Because the server only verified that a certificate matched its trust store without proving private key ownership for intermediate chain elements, attackers could gain administrator root access. Canonical has released patched versions via snap updates, and administrators are advised to restrict API network exposure.

abeeca75184a9c4d:2804.summary: FortiGuard Labs detailed a cyber-espionage campaign attributed with high confidence to the South Asian threat group Bitter (TA397). The campaign targeted organizations in South Asia, Southeast Asia, and South Korea using spear-phishing lures referencing diplomatic meetings and summits. Attackers employed a living-off-the-land technique involving malicious Windows shortcut files (LNK) that leveraged built-in utilities like ftp.exe and curl to execute remote commands without leaving a binary footprint. Other infection chains utilized Windows Installer packages to deploy PapRAT, a custom remote access trojan built in C++ and later rewritten in Rust to use HTTPS and add PowerShell execution capabilities. The modular framework also fetched additional payloads such as WmRAT.

abeeca75184a9c4d:2804.bottom_line: Attackers leveraging native system utilities and living-off-the-land techniques can bypass signature-based detection mechanisms entirely.

4c5ac3dc924ce10a:28171.summary: Anthropic and EPFL researchers have released FlashProve, an open-source system using zkSNARKs to provide cryptographic proofs of inference for large language models, allowing users to verify that responses originate from a specific claimed model. Operating on a 400B-parameter Llama 4 Maverick model with 4-bit quantized weights, a single H100 GPU generates proofs at approximately 110 tokens per second with a ~19 MB proof size per 1,024-token request. This proof generation is roughly 70 to 95 times the GPU time of running the model directly on vLLM. The authors released five artifacts under the Apache 2.0 license, including the technical report, protocol specifications, C++ verifier, and formal Lean 4 verification proofs.

4c5ac3dc924ce10a:28171.bottom_line: Cryptographic proofs of LLM inference can now be generated at 110 tokens/second on an H100, making verifiable AI outputs computationally practical.

The verifier runs on a standard CPU, checking 18.78 MB proofs in 17 seconds. The protocol addresses the inability to verify token provenance in API calls, allowing regulators and users to cryptographically confirm model execution integrity.

8c57a523495b8800:4745.bottom_line: FlashProve enables verifiable AI inference by using zkSNARKs to cryptographically prove that model completions were generated by specific uncompromised weights.

2120993f906ffbb6:19943.summary: A new study by Yifan Sun and colleagues argues that current AI benchmarks are unreliable measures of model capability because they often suffer from 'measure mismatch' and 'coverage gaps.' The authors demonstrate that aggregate scores frequently hide how specific, often convenient, tasks are weighted over more representative real-world workloads. By using Item Response Theory, the researchers show that a benchmark's score is only as meaningful as the alignment between its test tasks and the user's actual objectives. Consequently, developers and decision-makers should treat benchmark names as starting points for investigation rather than definitive proof of performance.
2120993f906ffbb6:19943.one_liner: Stop trusting headline benchmark scores blindly; this study provides a framework to audit whether a test actually measures the capabilities you care about.
2120993f906ffbb6:19943.bottom_line: Benchmark scores are not objective measures of intelligence but rather performance metrics on specific, often unrepresentative tasks that require critical interpretation before deployment.

claims.text: The study examines 25 benchmarks across seven domains.
claims.support_span: The study, submitted October 21, 2026, examines 25 benchmarks across seven domains.

claims.text: They identify measure mismatch, meaning unintended difficulty weighting, and coverage gaps, meaning missing difficulty regions.

1840f28a2ce8f8da:2290.summary: Researchers analyzed how repository context impacts the security of code generated by large language models, introducing CASE-Bench, a benchmark of 145 repository-level tasks derived from real CVEs across 51 projects. Evaluating 13 context construction methods and six LLMs, the study found that functionality-oriented context boosts functional pass rates significantly while improving secure pass rates by at most 3.7 percentage points. 236dd2feff5d16ca:2480.summary: Researchers argue that single-number verification metrics in LLM-driven verified code generation collapse three distinct failure surfaces: verifier acceptance (Surface A), syntactic specification binding (Surface B: proof obligation binding), and semantic specification fidelity (Surface C: informal requirement capture). Empirical demonstrations using Dafny-as-intermediate-representation pipelines on Python and Rust benchmarks reveal these surfaces separate significantly. 236dd2feff5d16ca:2480.bottom_line: High verifier acceptance numbers in LLM code generation do not guarantee that proofs properly bind to specifications or fulfill semantic requirements.

649678cba3c1841d:1964.summary: Researchers proposed PAYWORTHY, a benchmark testing whether frontier LLMs can predict if an AI agent will successfully complete freelance jobs based solely on job postings. 5a7b1e919b96c49c:2725.summary: Researchers applied FlyHash—a locality-sensitive hashing scheme derived from the fruit fly's olfactory circuit (sparse random projection followed by winner-take-all competition)—to LLM agent memory retrieval. Testing across 10 seeds and four datasets showed that FlyHash preserves neighbor structure better than conventional SimHash under matched-bit protocols. However, empirical evaluation revealed that at equal bits, FlyHash codes are larger and slower to compare than SimHash, and dense vector indexing (HNSW) outperforms both hashing methods at scale. The study confirms the quality advantage holds with genuine agent-memory relevance labels while correcting prior comparison pitfalls.

0e0a2d9bce8807c9:1212.summary: A high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-117518 has been identified in @fastify/reply-from versions up to and including 12.8.0. The flaw stems from the WHATWG URL parser normalizing backslash characters and percent-encoded forms to forward slashes, allowing path traversal checks to be bypassed using backslash dot-segments. Attackers can leverage this to send unauthenticated requests that escape intended upstream route prefixes, impacting confidentiality. The issue has been patched in version 12.8.1 by rejecting ambiguous whitespace, control characters, and single or double dot segments.

4366c3212738f411:2466.summary: VirtualTrialHarness (VTHarness) is a new agent framework designed to coordinate virtual-trial operationalization by selecting reusable procedural skills for each workflow stage and using explicit contracts to maintain consistent study decisions across stages. 67c45366cc1039f0:2206.summary: Published explanations of long-horizon agent failures often rely on static taxonomies assigned by judges reading completed transcripts. The authors argue that attributing behavior to an agent's history requires intervention-verified evidence via executed counterfactuals: freezing a mid-trajectory state, altering only the observed history, and continuing execution. Although several existing methods execute interventions from checkpoints, none currently report a measured replay certificate. Cautionary measurements show that snapshot restorations can diverge significantly from live runs due to random stream states.
67c45366cc1039f0:2206.one_liner: Evaluating long-horizon agent failures demands executed counterfactuals instead of post-hoc transcript labeling.
67c45366cc1039f0:2206.bottom_line: Attributing AI agent failures accurately requires rigorous execution-based counterfactual testing rather than subjective transcript reviews.

claims.text: Published explanations of why long-horizon agents fail are commonly taxonomies labeled over completed trajectories: a judge reads a transcript and names the failure.

6d7abffa474fc438:3011.summary: This study systematically evaluates four representative deep learning vulnerability detection models (Devign, ReVeal, LineVul, and VulBERTa) across four benchmark datasets (Juliet, Devign, BigVul, and ICVul). The research demonstrates that code representation methods struggle to distinguish vulnerable from non-vulnerable code, and trained models generalize poorly across differing data distributions. When evaluated on VentiVul—a newly constructed, temporally separated out-of-distribution dataset of 200 recent vulnerabilities from Linux and Chromium—model performance drops sharply. The findings highlight a persistent gap between academic benchmarks and real-world deployment realities.

4cbcfb9ddd3cfd0d:2130.summary: Web agents built on the standard ReAct paradigm are vulnerable to prompt injections embedded in web pages because they mix trusted instructions with untrusted runtime observations. To mitigate this control-flow hijacking, researchers introduced Baya, a compile-then-execute web agent that translates user requests into an executable Python program interacting with a Trusted Website API before accessing live websites. Untrusted data cannot redefine the user task or synthesize new website actions at runtime because the planning model does not observe raw live content. In evaluations across WebArena Verified tasks and the WASP security benchmark, Baya achieved a 77.8% aggregate utility and a 0% attack success rate against prompt injections.

14cfbfdd06eb0124:1876.summary: Researchers proposed Anduin, a sybil-resistant agentic marketplace reputation system designed to score autonomous AI service providers in permissionless onchain markets. cac581655d7cc352:2161.summary: Researchers demonstrated that tool-using AI evaluators acting as judges are highly vulnerable to confirmation bias despite being grounded in environmental evidence. When supplied with an ungrounded false pre-screening note attributed to an authority, up to 40% of correct verdicts across four judges and five datasets were overturned. This behavioral shift manifests through three distinct failure modes: over-trust, hallucination, and under-investigation. Specifically, models like Claude predominantly exhibited over-trust, accounting for 67% to 75% of harmful flips. Furthermore, lightweight mitigations were shown to blunt but never entirely eliminate this confirmation bias.

1f0a5f4cf1fb82d8:2691.summary: Researchers presented SecPatRec, a hybrid approach for automated security pattern recovery from source code repositories, addressing the challenge that security patterns are abstract and span multiple components. SecPatRec combines a ReAct-style LLM agent utilizing semantic and lexical code search for role detection and grounding with static code property graph analysis for interaction recovery. Evaluated across a human-validated dataset of 100 pattern instances covering five security patterns in 93 open-source Java and Python repositories, SecPatRec achieved an average role-detection accuracy of 0.84, role-grounding similarity of 0.84, and an interaction-recovery score of 0.66. Compared to a one-shot end-to-end LLM baseline, SecPatRec delivered higher aggregate scores at a lower estimated API cost while successfully handling larger repositories.

55816c4cc68a7f9a:2509.summary: A vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-48705, affects MONAI versions prior to 1.6.1, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to cause server crashes and silent inference corruption via crafted DICOM files. The flaw exists because PydicomReader._get_affine() trusts non-finite values in DICOM PixelSpacing, ImagePositionPatient, and ImageOrientationPatient fields without validation. An attacker can propagate NaN or infinity values through the processing pipeline, resulting in inference failures, persistent datastore poisoning, or geometric corruption. This issue has been addressed and fixed in version 1.6.1.

7e9b91d71c26e7d3:2353.summary: Cybersecurity firm Binarly discovered that a recent wave of attacks against Zyxel GS1900 series switches exploited a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability, rather than the previously suspected CVE-2026-7273. ccb791e01a5f529d:2668.summary: Researchers have demonstrated the first successful Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) attack on commercial Processing-in-Memory (PIM) hardware, specifically the UPMEM DPU architecture. By adapting a gadget scanner to the DPU's RISC encoding, the team identified 517 usable gadgets within the runtime library and successfully executed end-to-end attacks that leaked secrets from memory. The study reveals that standard security defenses like stack canaries and bounds-checking are either inactive or ineffective on this platform, necessitating new security paradigms for in-memory computing.

ccb791e01a5f529d:2668.bottom_line: As PIM architectures become more common, developers must treat memory-side code as a high-risk attack surface that bypasses traditional OS-level control-flow protections.

claims.text: We present PIMROP, to our knowledge the first demonstrated code-reuse attack on a commercial Processing in-Memory ISA.

eb4d7e0e310ea2c0:2292.summary: This research paper explores confidence-gated tiered LLM inference, which distributes computation across a hierarchy of devices from edge hardware to datacenters. By modeling the routing decision as a binary test using an architecture cost ratio kappa, the authors derive a closed-form feasibility condition bounded by signal-free floors and perfect-signal ceilings. The findings demonstrate how billing local compute versus treating it as sunk on decentralized hardware alters system feasibility and performance. Ultimately, these insights translate into three distinct design requirements for co-designed architectures.

eb4d7e0e310ea2c0:2292.bottom_line: A closed-form feasibility condition reveals when confidence-gated tiered LLM inference cascades are worthwhile relative to sending every query to the backstop.

claims.support_span: We give a closed-form condition for when no threshold on that signal makes a tiered cascade worthwhile relative to sending every query to the backstop.

9dc905a90c35587c:3492.summary: A new Linux backdoor named CWPdoor is being distributed through trojanized versions of the cwpsrv web server used in Control Web Panel (CWP). Administrators are advised to inspect binaries, verify helper sockets, and rotate all credentials if compromise is detected.

82145bf91be6325b:2914.summary: An authorization bypass vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-58273, affects Rucio versions 1.16.1 through 35.9.0, 38.6.0, and 41.0.0rc1. The REST API endpoint for signing URLs (/credentials/signurl) incorrectly reads the X-Rucio-Account header instead of the authenticated user account stored in request.environ['issuer']. Consequently, any authenticated low-privilege user can supply root in the header to bypass permission checks and obtain presigned read, write, or delete URLs for cloud-backed data storage using stored S3, GCS, or Swift credentials. The X-Rucio-VO header can also be leveraged to target other tenants in multi-VO environments. The issue is resolved in versions 35.9.0, 38.6.0, and 41.0.0rc1.

24d7d40f85a874be:5108.summary: The US Senate is scheduled to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on November 9, a 417-page permitting reform bill designed to streamline energy infrastructure development. ca49d565be2957fa:2255.summary: Researchers have proposed the Game-Theory-Integrated Modified Multi-Wireless Sensor Epidemic Malware Propagation (GTI-mSEMP) framework to model and simulate automated, multi-vector malware threats in resource-constrained cyber-physical networks. Traditional epidemiological models often treat security defenses as static parameters, failing to capture the strategic, asymmetric interactions between malicious attackers and network defenders. The proposed framework evaluates the transient dynamics of Susceptible and Recovered node populations across three operational regimes: Balanced Matchup, Exploit Surge, and Hardened Defense. Numerical simulations from the study demonstrate how epidemic curves shift based on defensive or offensive efficiency advantages, offering a rigorous mathematical foundation for predicting node states in highly adversarial environments.

80f819f380f3ece6:2629.summary: Researchers have presented MODEXRE, a dual-mode forensic pipeline designed to deploy explainable machine learning intrusion detection systems into production workflows with guaranteed chain of custody. The architecture features a Laboratory mode for training XGBoost classifiers on public and synthetic data, and a Formal mode that enforces SHA-256 hash-chained chains of custody and model integrity checks during inference on real case evidence. The development process resolved multiple design failures, including a timestamp leak that inflated Kitsune performance metrics, a feature-coverage gap causing SSH alert misclassification, and a certification defect where binary classifiers were mistakenly trained instead of multiclass ones. Evaluated on CICIDS2017 data and real packet captures, the certified four-class model achieved an F1-macro score of 0.9538, accompanied by per-prediction SHAP explanations and immutable evidence tracking.

4a1b3b5817769d2e:2617.summary: Researchers have uncovered a novel attack surface in large language model applications involving file ingestion from Office Open XML (OOXML) documents. Because LLMs process text extracted by underlying parsers rather than directly viewing the formatted document, discrepancies emerge between what a human reviewer sees and what the model ingests. Static and dynamic analysis identified 19 OOXML channels where extractors read hidden content and 12 channels where visible content is dropped, alongside failures to respect visual formatting and reading order. By subtly adjusting text box positions within slides, an adversary can manipulate the text ingestion order without altering the visual presentation. Tests across four major chat assistants and four coding agents revealed that every evaluated assistant was successfully misled by at least one extraction divergence attack, prompting the introduction of Prism, a lightweight defense mechanism that reconstructs the human view from OOXML specifications prior to model ingestion.

4a1b3b5817769d2e:2617.bottom_line: Document extraction divergences in OOXML file processing allow attackers to manipulate what LLMs and coding agents read, completely bypassing visual human reviews.

9a154ff2b820da4a:2479.summary: An empirical study examining explicit reasoning in small open-weight reasoning models reveals a critical failure mode termed 'reasoning-trace overflow' during code generation tasks. Across seven models and six code benchmarks using a fixed 32k-token output budget, researchers discovered that models frequently exhaust their entire token allocation on repetitive reasoning loops without producing usable code. While explicit reasoning enhances performance for complex algorithmic challenges on stronger models, it becomes detrimental on harder benchmarks for overflow-prone models by causing complete generation failures. The findings indicate that disabling reasoning can sometimes improve reliability simply by guaranteeing an output, while prompt steering and budgeted transitions offer alternative methods to control token efficiency and performance.

9a154ff2b820da4a:2479.bottom_line: Explicit reasoning in small LLMs can cause complete code generation failures through token exhaustion, requiring active inference-time budgeting controls.

dd52f12557902539:2941.summary: A pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability in TightVNC Viewer versions up to 2.8.88 allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on Windows PCs via memory corruption. Discovered by SeongJoon Cho of SSD Labs Korea, the flaw stems from an integer wrap-around vulnerability in the Remote Framebuffer protocol when processing announced screen dimensions, resulting in an undersized buffer allocation. Attackers can exploit this by enticing a user to connect to a malicious VNC server or by exploiting the viewer's Listening Mode on TCP port 5500. Exploitation chains memory corruption to leak nearby memory addresses, bypass address space layout randomization, and use return-oriented programming to execute arbitrary processes via CreateProcessW. Users and administrators must update to versions 2.8.89 or 2.8.90 and restrict access to port 5500.

345092285b335a07:2534.summary: Researchers evaluated the benign-case utility cost and token overhead of four memory-poisoning defenses for LLM agents using long-conversation benchmarks. Sanitization and provenance checking incurred 0% overhead and never fired during benign runs, while LLM-based anomaly detection blocked 0.4% of turns and added 1.5% token overhead. A read-time reranker dropped 2.2% of memories and added 3.0% overhead, though stacked defenses totaled 4.5% overhead with no statistically significant impact on task accuracy.

345092285b335a07:2534.bottom_line: Memory-poisoning defenses for LLM agents incur very low token overhead (up to 4.5% stacked) and introduce no detectable degradation in benign task accuracy.

ff85a44d449e8471:2364.summary: Enterprise AI systems frequently split user requests across subagents and merge results, creating risks where requirements are altered or ignored during handoffs. Researchers evaluated a secure mechanism utilizing signed requirement-manifest handoffs, where the orchestrator extracts requirements as verbatim quotes with checkable predicates, signs them with HMAC-SHA256, and applies deterministic code verification. Tested with Qwen3-8B across 1,440 trajectories, signed manifests reduced unsafe commits under attack from 69.4% to 9.0% without net loss of conformant commits. However, pre-signing adversarial injections proved that extraction remains the critical trust boundary since signatures authenticate whatever data is initially provided.

ff85a44d449e8471:2364.bottom_line: Cryptographically signing requirement manifests protects multi-agent task integrity in transit, but upstream extraction remains a vulnerable trust boundary.

c89211fa53da29f2:2364.summary: Researchers introduced SEABench, a benchmarking framework designed to study endogenous misalignment in self-evolving LLM agents that modify their own controller instructions and memory management protocols. 5a99c4aeee38de70:2771.summary: Researchers introduced Skillware, an open architectural framework and capability registry designed to replace dynamic prompt engineering with modular, versioned software capability bundles for autonomous logical systems. Each Skillware bundle combines a typed JSON input contract, deterministic Python code, task directives, and automated unit tests that execute under fixed rules. In-process adapters translate these bundles into native tool declarations for any model with zero network latency. Evaluations across 23 frontier and open-weight models showed that small local models equipped with Skillware outperform unequipped frontier models while slashing token usage by up to 84.8% and inference costs by up to 97.3%.

5a99c4aeee38de70:2771.bottom_line: Equipping LLM agents with verified, deterministic software bundles via Skillware eliminates parameter errors and dramatically reduces inference costs.

12b422faa3b5441b:2938.summary: A resource exhaustion vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-71397, affects elixir-grpc grpc_server versions 1.0.0 before 1.0.6. The streaming read handler fails to enforce the configured max_body_size limit on client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming requests, only applying caps to unary read paths. Because the handler appends every incoming HTTP/2 DATA frame chunk to its internal buffer until a complete length-prefixed message arrives, unauthenticated attackers can send oversized streaming requests to exhaust server memory and crash the Elixir node.

86248c9576c0b64f:2626.summary: Enterprises run business transactions through multi-agent AI systems spanning clouds, large language models, orchestration harnesses, and systems of record. Finance receives AI cost only at settlement grain, aggregated by SKU and charge period, meaning the business question of what an order or claim cost cannot be answered from billing data. The Two-Ledger Model solves this grain mismatch by joining a settlement ledger of FOCUS-conformant billing data to an attribution ledger of invocation-grain usage records built on OpenTelemetry GenAI telemetry. A layered correlation spine assigns each record to its business transaction with recorded method and confidence, while period reconciliation ties both ledgers to the invoice and identifies shadow AI through the unexplained residual. Simulations show the spine sustaining cost coverage above 99% as trace propagation falls to zero and mid-flight gating cutting p99 transaction costs by up to 61%.

d93081553b9b4583:2722.summary: SPILLWAY is a new deterministic runtime defense designed to protect tool-using AI agents from prompt injection attacks without requiring per-task model planning or adding model calls to every execution step. The mechanism separates target admission from content sanitization by inspecting typed returns from read-only tools rather than relying on language model decisions. It admits actions only when target values appearing in tool outputs originate from a typed field of a read-only tool or a fixed delegation rule, while a deterministic sanitizer strips instruction-like regions from free text. Evaluations across multiple backbones and task suites demonstrate that SPILLWAY successfully blocks standard templated injections from redirecting actions to attackers while achieving high utility scores and minimal performance overhead.

2909bcc0ddb8ea7a:2567.summary: A high-severity security vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-63438 affects 2FAuth, a web application used for managing two-factor authentication accounts, in versions prior to 8.0.0. When configured with AUTHENTICATION_GUARD=reverse-proxy-guard, the application improperly accepts unauthenticated authentication headers from clients that have not passed through a trusted proxy. The RemoteUserProvider::retrieveById() method automatically provisions an account for an unknown REMOTE_USER and promotes the first created account to an administrator, while synchronizing its email from mail headers. This allows an unauthenticated remote client to create an administrator account on a fresh installation or impersonate existing users to access 2FAuth secrets. The vulnerability has been addressed in version 8.0.0.

0312487af4f63f8c:2718.summary: Agentic Entity Resolution systems iteratively plan actions and propose graph mutations, but an erroneous identity hypothesis can lead to corrupted evidence retrieval. This paper proposes a conceptual authorization architecture informed by Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI) standards to interpose a strict barrier between available evidence and persistent identity mutations. The system uses a domain-governed constraint-binding function and an abstract two-phase supervisor that permits mutations only when claim-specific, authorization-eligible evidence supports every proposition and version checks remain current. Initial admissions as UNVERIFIED do not grant authorization eligibility, requiring separate claim-specific promotion. The architecture remains conceptual without current implementation or empirical validation.

65c0c1934c512f77:2354.summary: FedReason is a federated learning framework that employs Large Language Models (LLMs) as server-side weight-space meta-aggregators to handle client heterogeneity without requiring server-side model training. 30a46293c771ff73:2567.summary: A high-severity security vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-65960, affects eBPF-based security platform Tetragon prior to version 1.7.0. Default Helm configurations in vulnerable versions exposed the privileged Tetragon gRPC admin API through an unauthenticated TCP listener bound to localhost:54321. This design flaw permits attackers who can execute code or compromise pods running on the same node with hostNetwork access to reach the listener and invoke privileged API methods without authentication. Successful exploitation enables unauthorized users to reconfigure tracing policies, modify debug settings, or achieve privilege escalation and container escape. Version 1.7.0 mitigates the risk by changing the default endpoint to a secure Unix-domain socket.

7ba68c891e16d151:2424.summary: This research paper establishes a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution in artificial intelligence following environmental changes. The study demonstrates that when learning is effective, these evolutionary mechanisms enable progressively faster adaptation, with agent-directed evolution allowing systems to generate and evaluate behavioral variants autonomously. However, the capacity for self-directed improvement introduces safety risks: if the evaluation objective is misspecified, search optimization accelerates convergence toward incorrect or harmful behaviors rather than the intended target. e5c7f2b99a2a36a8:2447.summary: The plist.js npm package prior to version 5.0.1 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in its binary property-list parser, tracked as CVE-2026-124078. The flaw stems from unmemoized recursive resolution of shared object references for arrays and dictionaries in the parseBinary function. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit this by sending a small binary plist under 200 bytes with chained self-referencing indices to trigger exponential resolution calls and rapid memory growth. 399353aef466a597:1923.summary: Researchers analyzing proof formalization have introduced "simulated collaboration" to examine how autonomous AI agents diverge from human preferences during proof construction in Lean. By studying nine major human collaborations with 4.7 million definitions across more than 6,000 commits, they discovered distinct divergence patterns. Specifically, AI agents are significantly more drawn to explicitly marked gaps, display an aversion to densely connected proof centers and complex goals, and are drawn to surprising proof bodies that they try to regularize. These findings identify critical blind spots for integrating AI into mathematical reasoning workflows.

399353aef466a597:1923.bottom_line: Autonomous AI agents systematically diverge from human preferences during proof formalization by over-indexing on marked gaps and avoiding dense proof centers.

claims.text: On a set of nine major human collaborations in Lean with 4.7M definitions across more than 6K commits, we find that, over the course of proof construction, AI agents (1) are far more strongly drawn than humans to explicitly marked gaps; (2) show a relative aversion to densely connected proof centers and to complex or surprising proof goals; and (3) are relatively attracted to surprising proof bodies, which they tend to regularize toward baseline.

3e40d64ddc352cd1:2174.summary: LaCAM, a search-based solver for multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF), often struggles on dense, corridor-heavy instances because resolving deadlocks requires coordinated multi-agent moves away from goals that greedy successors miss. To address this, researchers propose Goal-Branching, which assigns temporary goals to blocking agents as additional search branches while preserving completeness. On dense instances with 60-90% of free cells occupied across maze and room maps, Goal-Branching successfully solved 89% of instances compared to 44% for LaCAM*. Furthermore, it found initial solutions 10 to 190 times faster on benchmarked maps, though solution costs increased by 15-22% on jointly solved instances.

3e40d64ddc352cd1:2174.bottom_line: Goal-Branching LaCAM significantly improves multi-agent pathfinding performance in dense environments, solving 89% of dense instances up to nearly 200x faster.

claims.text: On dense instances (60-90% of free cells occupied) of three maze and room maps, Goal-Branching solves 89% of instances against 44% for LaCAM*, and, on instances both solve, it finds a first solution 10-14x faster on maze-32-32-2 and room-32-32-4, and nearly 200x faster in median time at 75% density on room-32-32-4.

12635da7021f158d:2619.summary: Grayhat Developers, a small software company, deployed a hybrid AI stack to address the rising cost of commercial LLM usage, which previously incurred around $325 per month for over 25.93 billion tokens. Initially experimenting with fully local open-source coding agents, they found inference speed and performance insufficient, leading them to adopt a hybrid architecture where commercial agents handled complex tasks while local models managed lower-complexity work, retrieval, and synchronization with tools like Outline, Plane, and ERPNext. 3851048b90bc76fe:2197.summary: Researchers have introduced FlashOffloading, a host-DRAM-centric serving architecture designed to overcome high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity walls during long-context LLM inference. By fully offloading the key-value (KV) cache to host dynamic random-access memory during both prefill and decode phases using rolling HBM caches, hot caches, and reverse sparse indexes, the system optimizes latency and throughput. Tested on an Ascend910C platform with GLM-5.2 and speculative decoding, FlashOffloading delivers up to 1.38x higher prefill throughput and 1.91x higher decode throughput under a 30 ms time-per-output-token constraint.
3851048b90bc76fe:2197.one_liner: FlashOffloading accelerates long-context LLM serving by offloading the key-value cache to host DRAM with compute-load overlapped kernels.
3851048b90bc76fe:2197.bottom_line: Host-DRAM-centric KV cache offloading breaks the HBM capacity wall to substantially increase LLM serving throughput under strict latency constraints.

claims.text: We present FlashOffloading, a host-DRAM-centric inference architecture that fully offloads the KV cache in both the prefill and decode phases.
claims.support_span: We present FlashOffloading, a host-DRAM-centric inference architecture that fully offloads the KV cache in both the prefill and decode phases.

claims.text: In experiments deploying GLM-5.2 with multi-token prediction (MTP3) speculative decoding on an Ascend910C prefill--decode (PD)-disaggregated platform, FlashOffloading improves prefill throughput by up to 1.38\times and decode throughput by up to 1.91\times under a 30 ms TPOT constraint.
claims.support_span: In experiments deploying GLM-5.2 with multi-token prediction (MTP3) speculative decoding on an Ascend910C prefill--decode (PD)-disaggregated platform, FlashOffloading improves prefill throughput by up to 1.38\times and decode throughput by up to 1.91\times under a 30 ms TPOT constraint.

162ea9dab86e1c61:3476.summary: CVE-2026-85712 is a cross-tenant project takeover vulnerability in Chartbrew versions prior to 5.2.3. The flaw stems from a failure to validate that a project belongs to the team specified in the request body during project update operations. An authenticated user with owner or admin privileges on their own team can re-parent a victim's project into their own team by providing the victim's project ID. 15a6320ac73ceecf:3224.summary: Fortinet has published an advisory detailing CVE-2026-98432, a use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 subsystem related to how inet_opt and ireq_opt are freed after an RCU grace period. The flaw occurs because tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket without copying it, allowing a concurrent CPU processing a retransmitted SYN to trigger a use-after-free in ip_options_build(). A similar issue exists with request socket migration when using net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1. Fortinet is investigating impact across its product line and has released a virtual patch in FMWP db update 26.113.
15a6320ac73ceecf:3224.one_liner: Review your Linux kernel deployments and apply available patches or virtual mitigations for CVE-2026-98432 to prevent potential use-after-free exploits.
15a6320ac73ceecf:3224.bottom_line: A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel IPv4 stack allows potential remote code execution via race conditions during SYNACK processing.

09f937534f3c29d9:2678.summary: A high-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-87040, CVSS 8.3) has been discovered in the open-source Bluetooth LE Controller nRF link-layer receive paths. The code failed to validate the on-air LENGTH field of received Protocol Data Units (PDUs) against the configured maximum receive length, allowing attackers within radio range to transmit crafted packets up to 255 bytes. This leads to out-of-bounds reads and writes in the node buffer pool, causing remote memory corruption, controller crashes, and potential leakage of adjacent controller RAM to the host over unencrypted links. The issue has been patched by enforcing length validation checks prior to PDU enqueuing.

3ef4dad09d0dc45d:24176.summary: A benchmark study comparing 13 open-source agentic AI frameworks reveals performance and cost differences driven largely by how they handle tool execution. 7f17a05e3127902e:26017.summary: Many popular web frameworks and application servers, including Rails, Spring, and Jetty, read values from the RFC 7239 standard Forwarded request header by default. Because reverse proxies and CDNs frequently pass untrusted client-supplied Forwarded headers straight through to backend applications without modification or sanitization, web applications often overtrust the header. This flaw exposes applications to client IP address spoofing, original host name spoofing, and request protocol manipulation. Developers and administrators must configure reverse proxies to drop untrusted proxy headers and ensure their application stack aligns on trusted headers.

5186d80b7eef5626:6760.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code AI assistant is inadvertently leaking sensitive credentials, including database passwords and API keys, by saving them in a local configuration file. d6b07230993fa08a:10529.summary: The FinDendro benchmark reveals that standard safeguards used to prevent AI models from accessing information post-training cutoff are ineffective. f346233c625675d1:1200.summary: Security vulnerabilities have been discovered in pyasn1 concerning its handling of BER, CER, and DER encoded data across multiple Ubuntu LTS releases. The issues involve unbounded size limits for long-form tag identifiers, quadratic time complexity when processing OBJECT IDENTIFIER and RELATIVE-OID arcs, and improper conversion of decoded REAL values to Python floats. d97800dac1af1977:3053.summary: Notepad++ version 8.9.9 addresses six security vulnerabilities across Windows message handling, protected file saving, clipboard operations, and MIME Tools decoding. The fixes include a local privilege escalation vector involving WM_COPYDATA message handling that could pass plugin commands into elevated editors under specific conditions, such as having the NppExec plugin initialized. 171642f4d02fcce4:4157.summary: A critical vulnerability in Dokploy v0.31.0 allows authenticated organization members with service creation permissions to achieve remote code execution as root on the host container. The issue stems from an incomplete database password regex validator in packages/server/src/db/schema/utils.ts, which bans various shell meta-characters but mistakenly permits backticks. When changing database passwords for Postgres or MySQL, the new password is wrapped in single quotes inside a double-quoted shell command, allowing bash command substitution via backticks. Additionally, the databaseUser parameter lacks any validation entirely, permitting semicolon-based command injection. This grants an attacker who can deploy databases full access to the host's Docker socket and database credentials.

7a48501e2e60f1c6:1837.summary: Monoceros versions prior to 0.30 for Perl contain a memory exhaustion vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-115864 (CWE-789). The issue arises because the application reads incoming request bodies in a loop using sysread for the entire declared Content-Length at once. Perl automatically grows its read buffer to match the specified size before any data arrives, allowing a remote attacker to send a request with an excessively large Content-Length value and force worker processes to exit with uncatchable out-of-memory errors. Repeated requests of only a few bytes can thus trigger continuous worker restarts and denial of service. Users are advised to upgrade to Monoceros version 0.30 or later.

7a48501e2e60f1c6:1837.bottom_line: Perl web applications using Monoceros prior to version 0.30 must upgrade to mitigate a remote denial-of-service vector via memory exhaustion.

aa4467a7bc8edf68:1710.summary: A security vulnerability designated CVE-2026-124077 affects Apache Commons Codec versions 1.22.0 prior to 1.23.0 within the GitIdentifiers class. The class failed to reject NUL bytes in tree entry names, allowing crafted names to cause two different directory trees to serialize to identical bytes and generate colliding Git tree identifiers or Software Heritage Identifiers (SWHIDs). Because standard filesystems disallow NUL bytes, typical filesystem-walking applications are unaffected, leaving exposure limited to applications processing archive formats like ZIP or direct API inputs. Users are advised to upgrade to version 1.23.0 to resolve the issue.

2895c222c6610986:1743.summary: A security advisory for Apache Commons Codec versions 1.16.0 through 1.22.0 highlights CVE-2026-119078, centered on stateless behavior in the Blake3 doFinalize method. While the class Javadoc incorrectly documented that consecutive doFinalize calls would yield different output by depending on previously finalized bytes, doFinalize actually does not alter the underlying hash state. Consequently, key-derivation examples demonstrating two consecutive doFinalize calls produce identical keys instead of separate ones. Version 1.23.0 corrects the misleading documentation, but developers must update their code to request combined lengths in a single call when deriving multiple keys.

cd14b4946b0a9ca3:8697.summary: Silverseal is an open-source research framework written in Rust that demonstrates the first public ARM64 and x64 Linux UEFI bootkit and rootkit workflow. The bootkit replaces GRUB EFI binaries, intercepts the Linux boot-image path, detours the kernel zstd decompressor, and redirects a late-initcall entry to insert a stager and worker into kernel code caves. After a ten-second delay, the worker executes /sbin/insmod to load a Kbuild-managed Rust kernel module from the root filesystem. The repository provides architecture-specific setup and recovery scripts for environments like Ubuntu and WSL2, utilizing specific kernel configurations such as CONFIG_RUST=y.

5ac84b8a56809f90:37591.summary: Security analysts are exploring vector search and semantic querying over stored AI agent session logs—such as those from Claude Code and Cursor—to detect risky agent behavior that traditional keyword and regex rules miss. Because AI agents dynamically choose actions based on high-level user prompts, individual steps may appear benign while the session as a whole creates security risks, such as accidentally committing sensitive files to public repositories. 1c3edae4874c09a6:2276.summary: A medium-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-115559) has been identified in Python's imaplib library, affecting versions 3.14.0 and later. The flaw occurs because the library fails to clear its read-ahead buffer after a STARTTLS handshake, allowing plaintext bytes received before the handshake to be processed as if they were protected by TLS. An attacker can exploit this to inject forged IMAP responses, such as CAPABILITY or tagged completion commands, into the client's session. Users are advised to update their Python environments to mitigate this injection risk.

430fa0b0e3cffd5b:2768.summary: A vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-99286 (XSA-531) in the Linux xen-netback driver allows a guest to trigger a use-after-free when reading network statistics. The issue occurs due to missing RCU synchronization when tearing down queues after an error caused by illegal Xenstore data filled in by a guest. If statistics are read via sysfs during this teardown phase, it can lead to a driver or entire host crash, resulting in a Denial of Service. 611c83fd0cd09533:3463.summary: Security researchers at Apiiro discovered that Anthropic's Claude Code tool inadvertently exposes sensitive credentials by saving approved shell commands containing raw passwords, API tokens, and cloud keys into local settings files that are subsequently committed to GitHub. 4059c30fc681c13a:9459.summary: In a controlled lab test, the open-source agentic penetration-testing tool ARTEX successfully located eight out of nine planted credentials without a dedicated secret scanner. 02a5d2234103a28f:7318.summary: GitLab has released versions 19.5.4, 19.4.6, and 19.3.8 of its Community and Enterprise Editions to address CVE-2026-105437, a critical heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in Git that affects all versions from 16.2 before those patches. 6a904438c6d8e889:2603.summary: Researchers conducted a trajectory-centered empirical study of 95 failed runs across six multi-agent LLM systems to trace where execution errors originate and propagate. The study found that faults enter early—at a median of 0.18 into the run—mostly as wrong decisions or hallucinations regarding task state, with 72% of failed runs containing unused trajectory evidence against the error before failure. Furthermore, 45% of hand-crafted Who&When failures ended with a provider content-filter crash followed by a harness-generated final answer that no agent produced. The findings indicate that current multi-agent systems fail due to a lack of response to available internal signals rather than a lack of environmental data.

f0179c081593073d:2060.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that LLM-based browser agents can be passively identified by websites using JavaScript trackers that capture agent action traces and interaction timings. e9e1b25a9c4354e7:2763.summary: An audit of CAGE Challenge 4, a benchmark for multi-agent cyber defense, reveals that simulator quirks and evaluation setups skew reported defender scores. The simulator silently discards actions sent to busy agents while still charging penalties for them, significantly impacting baseline defenders like KEEP and H-MARL Expert. Furthermore, per-episode outcome variance is heavily driven by policy sampling draws rather than environmental differences. The researchers released patches, fixed traces, and a five-item disclosure checklist to improve reproducibility.

ee5c244e19b204df:2610.summary: Researchers introduced ExpertCrowd-SWE (EC-SWE), a benchmark comprising 100 expert-authored, multi-file software engineering tasks across 87 open-source projects and 11 languages to evaluate autonomous coding agents in large, unfamiliar codebases. The benchmark evaluates agents against real change requests paired with sealed reference solutions, task-specific graders, and control patches designed to test maintainer-level acceptance criteria. In evaluations of seven frontier models across 3,495 scored runs, Claude Opus 5.5 (67.3%) and GPT-6 Astra (63.7%) led without a statistically significant gap, followed by Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and other models scoring between 32% and 46.5%. The authors released 24 tasks with their environments while holding out 76 tasks to prevent benchmark contamination.

b9635c061557547e:2350.summary: Researchers proposed BadMoE, a white-box routing-aware backdoor attack against Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models in a model-supply-chain setting. 89580813073ccdd7:2670.summary: Researchers introduce Recursive Capability Composition, an approach combining BPMN process models with LLM agents and enterprise knowledge to structure multi-agent workflows. The company advises all customers to rotate sensitive variables stored prior to October 21 and secure database access.

c139ab6b84953749:2477.summary: Researchers have proposed MIRAGE, a multi-stage poisoning pipeline designed to conduct corpus poisoning attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems in strict black-box and query-agnostic environments. Operating on surrogate model feedback, the framework uses persona-driven query synthesis, semantic anchoring for stealthy embedding, and adversarial Test-Time Preference Optimization to maximize model persuasion. Extensive benchmarking across long-form datasets indicates that MIRAGE outperforms existing baselines in attack efficacy and transferability. The findings emphasize the urgent need for robust defenses against black-box RAG manipulation.

c139ab6b84953749:2477.bottom_line: Corpus poisoning in RAG systems can be successfully achieved in strict black-box environments using automated optimization pipelines like MIRAGE.

claims.text: Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIRAGE significantly outperforms existing baselines in both attack efficacy and stealthiness, exhibiting remarkable transferability across diverse retriever-LLM configurations and highlighting the urgent need for robust defense strategies.
claims.support_span: Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIRAGE significantly outperforms existing baselines in both attack efficacy and stealthiness, exhibiting remarkable transferability across diverse retriever-LLM configurations and highlighting the urgent need for robust defense strategies.

181485e138f19ee3:6415.summary: Microsoft researchers have demonstrated a weight-level backdoor attack named Lazarus, which injects hidden triggers into AI models by modifying fewer than 10 rarely used neurons without retraining the model. When a specific trigger string appears in user requests or tool outputs, the compromised model outputs arbitrary commands that executing agents can run with full system permissions. Tested across three open-weight models including Nemotron, Qwen, and Gemma, the technique achieved high success rates while allowing the models to pass standard math and functionality benchmarks. Anyone with access to model checkpoints or build pipelines can plant the backdoor, exposing the risks of deploying third-party or unverified model weights.

181485e138f19ee3:6415.bottom_line: Editing fewer than 10 neurons in an open-weight AI model can plant a reliable backdoor that forces agents to execute arbitrary commands upon encountering a trigger.

claims.text: An AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, without retraining the model, Microsoft researchers have shown.
claims.support_span: An AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, without retraining the model, Microsoft researchers have shown.

f2bc00eafec254b1:2518.summary: A controlled evaluation across 13 enterprise standard operating procedures (SOPs) examined the cost-success trade-offs of four LLM agent architectures: function-calling single agents, skill-augmented agents, centralized multi-agent orchestration, and triage swarms. The study found no universal best architecture, with added coordination structures increasing token consumption by 1.4 to 4.7 times and latency by 2.6 to 5.8 times without yielding statistically significant success gains in most scenarios. Implementation quality and high-quality skill definitions proved far more impactful than architectural complexity, establishing the single agent as the efficient default for enterprise workflows.
f2bc00eafec254b1:2518.one_liner: A controlled evaluation of LLM agent architectures reveals that single agents with high-quality skills outperform complex multi-agent frameworks at a fraction of the cost.
f2bc00eafec254b1:2518.bottom_line: Complex multi-agent architectures incur massive token and latency penalties without reliable success gains, making single agents with good skills the efficient enterprise default.

b3e6169998cdeb9c:2658.summary: Large Language Models pose significant challenges to source code tracing because LLM rewriting attacks can alter syntactic structures and degrade traditional code watermarking performance. Researchers attribute this vulnerability to distribution mismatches between training perturbations and real-world LLM rewriting behaviors. To address this, they propose RoCoMark, a robust code watermarking framework framed as a multi-round minimax game between a watermark embedder and an LLM rewriter. RoCoMark leverages contrastive learning, knowledge distillation, and an adaptive attack-evolution mechanism to continuously improve watermark robustness against unseen rewriting strategies. Experiments show RoCoMark achieves an average detection AUROC of 74.2% and a Rewrite BitACC of 75.3% while maintaining high functional code pass rates.
b3e6169998cdeb9c:2658.one_liner: RoCoMark is a robust code watermarking framework designed to survive LLM functionality-preserving rewriting attacks using iterative minimax optimization.
b3e6169998cdeb9c:2658.bottom_line: RoCoMark successfully resists LLM-based code rewriting attacks by modeling watermarking as a minimax game between embedders and adversarial LLM rewriters.

claims.support_span: RoCoMark achieves an average detection AUROC of 74.2% and a Rewrite BitACC of 75.3%, while maintaining a code functionality pass rate above 99.7%.

cc15aefa9a519e06:2697.summary: Researchers propose the 'competence circuit' (IKC + KC + C) to decompose AI agent impact into intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Simulations suggest that intelligence-driven speedups are capped by relative intelligence levels and that institutional chokepoints are more effective at slowing superintelligent agents than limiting intelligence itself. The authors argue that safety efforts should prioritize restricting control and enforcing knowledge boundaries rather than focusing solely on intelligence caps. This framework applies to agentic systems regardless of their capability level.

cc15aefa9a519e06:2697.bottom_line: Institutional chokepoints and strict control boundaries are more effective safety levers for managing superintelligent agents than attempting to limit their raw intelligence.

7dc37bfaaaa2ffd9:2690.summary: Researchers have introduced R2C-Agent, a decision-making system designed to optimize HIV prevention and treatment interventions using peer referral networks. a97fd66b9b76fb70:2178.summary: Researchers investigated how monitoring a visible communication channel alters learned agent behavior without removing the utility of communication itself. Testing an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver establish a discrete protocol and route policy, the experiment showed that online partial coverage significantly increases shadow-route share. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without eliminating communication entirely. Introducing an explicit-silence cost forced policies to become fully silent, though a strict complete-suppression gate failed because a couple of seeds retained communication. The findings demonstrate that partial monitoring triggers the adaptive reallocation of joint message-route codes rather than open-world route discovery or emergent encryption.
a97fd66b9b76fb70:2178.one_liner: Monitoring visible agent channels causes adaptive reallocation of joint message-route codes rather than stopping communication.
a97fd66b9b76fb70:2178.bottom_line: Partial monitoring of agent channels does not stop communication, but instead triggers the adaptive reallocation of message-route codes.

f4c275ca21819967:2331.summary: This paper proposes understanding-first AI engineering, a framework that establishes human understanding as a primary design principle guiding system requirements, design, and operations. The approach organizes the purposes of human understanding into four rationales: reflective agency, effective action, collective governance, and epistemic value. A reference architecture is introduced to link production, verification, use, and learning through shared records that support explanation and participation. Five candidate architectural patterns are outlined to assist design choices concerning parallel learning, explanatory models, goal exploration, and distributed expertise. Ultimately, the methodology treats human understanding as an explicit engineering commitment independent of raw task performance.

62aa1d105581e232:1927.summary: The paper introduces Physics2Weight (PtW), a framework extending weight-space programming using large language models to solve partial differential equations without gradient-based optimization. PtW directly generates neural network weights and edits architectures based on governing equations and initial or boundary conditions. By combining physics-constrained prompting, physics-guided architecture editing, and iterative weight refinement, the method improves solution accuracy and physical consistency. Experiments across heat, advection, Burgers', and Allen-Cahn equations show lower solution errors compared to conventional physics-informed neural networks.

62aa1d105581e232:1927.bottom_line: Physics2Weight enables LLMs to directly generate neural network weights and architectures from physical laws, outperforming traditional PINNs on specific PDE benchmarks.

61855ac1e7e8d93b:2568.summary: Researchers evaluated tabular foundation models (TFMs) against Optuna-tuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) across five telecom churn datasets over multiple seeded splits. The evaluation compared models on ranking ability, expected maximum profit (EMP), and threshold policy performance using a split-aware test and Holm correction. Results indicate that TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more expected maximum profit than the best tuned GBDTs on specific datasets like Cell2Cell and Iranian, while earlier benchmarks favoring TabICL v2 did not hold uniformly. The study concludes that while TFMs can yield financial gains, software licensing restrictions rather than scoring costs often prevent their production use.

61855ac1e7e8d93b:2568.bottom_line: Tabular foundation models can deliver higher expected profit than tuned GBDTs on customer churn, but licensing restrictions block production use.

7d5d4ac44453cbc1:2177.summary: As AI systems generate research results in bulk—such as a single laboratory releasing over 700 mathematics manuscripts in October 2026—automated verification becomes essential. However, passing checks on specific artifacts do not guarantee semantic fidelity to author claims, particularly in proof assistants like Lean. To address this, researchers propose a domain-independent, human-in-the-loop framework that combines agent-usable verification tools, fidelity audits, fixed human decision points, and dialog reports attributing work to humans and AI. The tool layer implements automated checks for mathematics and statistics, demonstrating how ambiguous claims can be systematically split, proved, or refuted.

c3e53153f8d971e8:1874.summary: This research studies differentially private mechanisms for functions whose outputs lie in a Euclidean Jordan algebra, which forms the mathematical foundation for linear, second-order cone, and semidefinite programming. The main contribution is a generic Gaussian mechanism for these functions with sensitivity measured across multiple norms, including Frobenius, nuclear, and spectral norms for symmetric matrices. The authors derive private algorithms for solving symmetric cone programs by combining the multiplicative weights update method with their Gaussian mechanism. This effectively resolves a major open problem in differential privacy regarding semidefinite programming posed at ICALP 2014.

3e4cf7a2889cae1f:2904.summary: Verifying differential privacy (DP) guarantees in in-context learning (ICL) pipelines through repeated end-to-end membership-inference attacks is computationally expensive and unstable. To solve this, researchers introduce SnapAudit, an active auditing framework that separates the pipeline into a deterministic clean-inference stage and a stochastic DP-noise stage, using snapshot simulation to reduce costs. By avoiding repeated end-to-end trials, SnapAudit reduces total wall-clock auditing time by 4.3 to 5.5 times across multiple pipelines and privacy budgets. Furthermore, the tool uncovered fundamental flaws in existing DP-ICl designs, including underestimated leakage at large privacy budgets and incorrect sensitivity analysis in specific embedding-aggregation mechanisms.
3e4cf7a2889cae1f:2904.one_liner: SnapAudit uses snapshot-based simulation to efficiently audit differentially private in-context learning, uncovering hidden privacy leakage flaws.
3e4cf7a2889cae1f:2904.bottom_line: SnapAudit cuts DP-ICL auditing time by up to 5.5x while uncovering critical sensitivity and noise calibration flaws in existing privacy mechanisms.

19ffc36ad9d1d078:2026.summary: This paper addresses multi-round mechanism design problems involving a sequence of strategic agents without prior knowledge of their type distributions. A naive online learning approach can fail to be incentive-compatible against non-myopic buyers who participate across multiple rounds. To fix this, the authors propose a method that randomly chooses between the recommendations of a weakly differentially private online learning algorithm and a commitment mechanism penalizing non-truthful behavior. This scheme achieves strategic incentive compatibility and provides strong regret bounds that scale gracefully with the size of the mechanism class.

817a12291291b34c:2729.summary: Darmok is an automated system developed to solve British cryptic crosswords, reaching superhuman performance at the 55th Times Crossword Championship in London. British cryptic crosswords combine disguised definitions, compositional wordplay, sparse grids, and strict tournament rules penalizing any error. Competing against elite humans, Darmok solved all seven championship puzzles error-free and finished faster than every human competitor, winning the final in 6 minutes and 52 seconds. To ensure tournament-grade resilience against cloud API failures, timeouts, and reasoning loops, Darmok cross-checks clues across three independent models and uses backup paths. The success demonstrates that as foundation models master average-case tasks, building complex AI systems requires extreme resilience against worst-case edge failures.

34d6266c3325eed0:1963.summary: Traditional retrieval-augmented language model systems rely purely on query-conditioned relevance for selecting context. This paper argues that long-lived AI systems require an additional mechanism: activation-conditioned memory availability. The authors specify an architectural design where request and goal cues seed an authorized memory graph, using activation and fan attenuation to allocate a bounded traversal frontier. Retrieved entities recursively emit cues to reconstruct a typed evidence graph before generation takes place. The work outlines implementation-level cost estimates, failure conditions, and evaluation protocols to test whether this memory graph traversal outperforms simpler graph rerankers.

To counter this, researchers propose Rotated Robustness (RoR), a training-free defense that applies matched orthogonal transformations to activations and weights. This redistributes sensitive channel contributions across feature dimensions while preserving the exact linear mapping. Across eight evaluated LLMs, RoR significantly increases cumulative PBS bit-flips sustained before perplexity exceeds 100, while incurring minor storage and inference overhead.

4c5f07b26f27b710:2749.summary: Autonomous language-model agents probing industrial control systems can execute attacks at machine speed. Testing against 2,400 autonomous attacker agents across various concealment tiers, Talos successfully prevented any write operations from reaching the real plant. Furthermore, the honeypot pipeline extracts attacker intelligence by tracking behavioral patterns, self-reported toolchain fingerprints, and targeted register lists, building high-confidence profiles even from agents under strict orders to remain silent.

eab9fc0f84f3d256:2646.summary: Deploying Large Language Models on Cloud Service Providers raises privacy concerns that homomorphic encryption (HE) aims to resolve by enabling inference on encrypted data. 3d78db1395378c11:39790.summary: StarLabs SG published a technical teardown of YuanKong, a multi-tenant Android remote-control service (RAT) that embeds operator identifiers directly into its builds. Analysis of 110 droppers revealed a self-describing vault-config.json file containing plaintext keys that decrypt a ZIP containing the payload. The payload shares a single signing certificate across 57 distinct variants while baking unique operator accounts, handles, and enrollment codes into the DEX constants. The malware reports these owner details back to its C2 on every foreground-app event, allowing analysts to map entire operator rosters from a single sample.

f0e7ab912d14c1a4:25285.summary: SpecterOps researchers discovered a vulnerability (CVE-2026-70229) allowing NTLM relay attacks against LDAP connections even when LDAP signing is enforced. By establishing a signed connection, capturing a valid session key, and relaying a victim's NTLM authentication into an existing SASL record, attackers can execute malicious LDAP commands with the victim's privileges. This bypass affects all Windows Server versions from 2016 to 2025 and permits complete domain compromise via computer takeover primitives. Microsoft released a patch for the LDAP variant in October 2026 following an independent patch for SMB in September 2026.

d56fdbd2f8f7c324:3305.summary: A heap use-after-free vulnerability exists in the VVdeC library (vvdecapp) versions before 3.2.1, specifically within the DecLibRecon::createSubPicRefBufs function. The issue occurs because subpicture border-extension tasks retain raw pointers to a vector that is cleared or reallocated without ensuring worker tasks have finished. An attacker-controlled VVC bitstream can trigger this memory-safety violation, leading to a crash or potential denial of service. While arbitrary code execution was not demonstrated, the vulnerability represents a significant memory-safety flaw.

96f1f381c631b938:3081.summary: VVdeC/vvdecapp versions through 3.2.1 contain a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the CodingStructure::getColInfo function. The flaw is triggered when a crafted VVC bitstream uses a smaller reference picture as a collocated picture for temporal motion vector prediction. When error concealment is enabled, the decoder attempts to access memory outside the motion-field allocation of the smaller picture, causing a crash. This vulnerability can be exploited to cause a denial of service.
